title: 1961 London County Council election
summary: The final election to the London County Council before it was absorbed into the new Greater London Council. Labour, in power at County Hall since 1934, retained a comfortable majority with 84 of the 126 elected seats. The Liberals enjoyed a modest revival, winning 6.0% of the vote.
highlights: Labour holds the LCC with 84 of 126 seats
The last-ever London County Council election
A Liberal revival lifts their vote share to 6.0%
Labour had controlled County Hall continuously since 1934

council.note: 126 directly elected councillors, plus aldermen chosen by the council. Seat shares are taken from Rallings & Thrasher's record of LCC results.

sources.label: Rallings & Thrasher, London County Council Elections 1889–1961 (Elections Centre)
